title: Fourier coefficients of a function far from low degree
statement:
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function, let $d\ge 1$, and let $\varepsilon$ satisfy $0\le\varepsilon\le 1$. Suppose $f$ is $\varepsilon$-far from degree $\le d$; that is, $\Pr_{x}[f(x)\ne g(x)]\ge\varepsilon$ for every Boolean function $g:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ of degree $\le d$. Writing $(-1)^f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ for the $\pm1$ lift of $f$ and $\widehat{(-1)^f}(S)=\E_x[(-1)^{f(x)}\chi_S(x)]$ for its Fourier coefficient at $S$, we then have, for every $S\subseteq[n]$,
\[
  \widehat{(-1)^f}(S)\;\le\;1-2\varepsilon.
\]
hypotheses_covered: f is ε-far from degree ≤ d: dist(f,g) ≥ ε for every Boolean g of degree ≤ d
